title: USAR Falls Below 50-Day SMA: Is It Time to Hold or Exit the Stock?
author: Na
description: USA Rare Earth (USAR) has fallen below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, declining 18.8% over six months due to continued operating losses, negative gross margins, and significant cash burn from capacity expansion. While the Serra Verde acquisition and up to $1.6B in government-backed funding provide growth opportunities, the company faces near-term profitability pressure and execution risks as it ramps commercial production.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company is trading below key moving averages, reporting significant operating losses ($83M), negative gross margins (-12.8%), and high cash burn ($75.3M in H1 2026). Despite strategic growth initiatives, near-term profitability remains challenged with execution risks in ramping production. Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating reflects these concerns.

title: NHYDY or BHP: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
author: Na
description: In a comparison of two mining stocks, Norsk Hydro ASA (NHYDY) emerges as the better value investment option compared to BHP. NHYDY holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with an A Value grade, supported by a lower forward P/E ratio of 11.13 versus BHP's 18.17, and a more favorable PEG ratio of 1.82 compared to BHP's 11.96. BHP carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a C Value grade.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: NHYDY has a superior Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) indicating positive earnings estimate revisions, an A Value grade, and more attractive valuation metrics including a lower forward P/E of 11.13, lower PEG ratio of 1.82, and lower P/B ratio of 1.7, making it the preferred choice for value investors.

BHP has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) and a C Value grade. While it is a legitimate mining company, its higher valuation multiples (forward P/E of 18.17, PEG ratio of 11.96, P/B ratio of 4.15) make it less attractive as a value investment compared to NHYDY.

title: Is Antamina Set to Boost Wheaton Precious Metals' Production?
author: Na
description: Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) has shown solid performance in 2026, driven by its $4.3 billion precious metals purchase agreement with BHP Group for the Antamina mine. The deal increased WPM's attributable silver to 67.5% and boosted Q2 silver production to 2.3 million ounces (up 56% year-over-year). WPM expects 2026 production of 860,000-940,000 GEOs and targets 1.2 million GEOs annually by 2030. However, WPM trades at a premium valuation (31.24X forward P/E vs. 17.16X industry average) and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While WPM shows strong production growth (56% YoY silver increase) and a landmark $4.3B Antamina deal, the stock carries a premium valuation (31.24X forward P/E) and a Hold rating. EPS estimates have declined over the past 60 days, and 2027 earnings are expected to dip 4.8%, offsetting near-term production gains.

BHP's Antamina mine is performing well with 56% YoY silver production growth, and the $4.3B PMPA with WPM represents a significant monetization of precious metals byproducts, providing stable long-term cash flows.

SSR Mining produced 101,959 gold-equivalent ounces in Q2 2026 with 2026 guidance of 450,000-535,000 ounces weighted to H2. No significant concerns or catalysts are highlighted, suggesting stable but unremarkable performance.

AngloGold Ashanti's gold production declined 4% YoY in H1 2026 due to the Serra Grande mine sale and operational challenges at Obuasi, including a contractor fatality. While H2 production is expected to improve, the company faces near-term headwinds.

title: Can Southern Copper's Investment Plan Fuel Long-Term Output Growth?
author: Na
description: Southern Copper Corporation (SCCO) announced a $20.5 billion investment plan over the next decade, with $10.3 billion allocated to three major Peruvian projects: Tía María, Los Chancas, and Michiquillay. The company expects production to reach 1.6 million tons by 2033-2034. SCCO shares have surged 123.3% year-to-date, significantly outperforming the mining industry average of 82.4%.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company announced substantial $20.5B investment commitment with clear project timelines and production targets. Stock has significantly outperformed peers and broader market. Strong long-term outlook with expected production growth to 1.6M tons. However, trading at premium valuation (29.17X forward P/E vs 24.84X industry average) and 2027 earnings expected to decline 8.2%.

Completed evaluation of large-scale El Abra expansion in Chile with potential to add 700+ million pounds of annual copper production. Strong liquidity profile and substantial cash flow generation provide flexibility for expansion and shareholder returns.

Has copper projects in execution pipeline expected to deliver ~2 Mtpa of attributable copper production by 2030s. Approved $0.5B pre-commitment funding for Escondida New Concentrator project with potential to add 230-270 kt of copper annually.

title: Un secteur résidentiel en plein essor stimule la croissance de la construction en Saskatchewan jusqu’en 2035, tandis que l’activité des grands projets non résidentiels fluctue
author: Construforce Canada
description: Saskatchewan's construction sector is expected to grow through 2035, driven primarily by strong residential construction and renovations. Non-residential activity will fluctuate based on major resource and infrastructure projects. The sector faces a potential labor shortage of 3,600 workers despite anticipated recruitment efforts, requiring strategies to attract workers from underrepresented groups and immigrants.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Jansen potash mine project is actively supporting construction activity in the short term, with Phase 2 expected to sustain high activity levels through 2031, providing significant employment opportunities.
AI data center project is mentioned as currently under study with potential for favorable investment decision, but remains speculative and not yet committed.
Wheeler River uranium project is anticipated to commence, contributing to near-term engineering and construction activity in Saskatchewan.
